title: When Disclosure Is Compulsory: Evaluating Ride-Hailing Rebalancing Policies with Self-Interested LLM Driver Agents
abstract: arXiv:2610.41132v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: The EU Platform Work Directive, to be transposed by December 2026, requires ride-hailing platforms to state in plain language the main parameters of their automated decisions and how a worker's behaviour affects them. Such rules are exactly what a large language model (LLM) can read, so drivers will be able to let one decide for them. We compare two main families of rebalancing policy once their rules are public: a reactive policy (R) that sends idle drivers to cover requests just lost, and an anticipatory policy (A) that plans moves on a demand forecast. Each driver is an LLM agent maximizing its own net income, given no rules (N) or the rules at the directive's level of detail (L). We test two LLMs, Claude Haiku 5.5 and Jev, which understand the rules equally well, in a three-zone model and in Manhattan. With the rules disclosed, drivers follow the platform more closely: in Manhattan, the share of relocation offers they decline falls

translated_title: 当披露成为强制要求：利用自利的大语言模型司机智能体评估网约车调度政策
translated_abstract: 欧盟《平台工作指令》将于2026年12月前转化为成员国法律，要求网约车平台以通俗易懂的语言说明其自动化决策的主要参数，以及劳动者行为如何影响这些决策。这类规则正是大语言模型（LLM）能够阅读的内容，因此司机将可以让LLM代替自己做决策。在规则公开之后，我们比较了两类主要的调度（rebalancing）政策：反应式政策（R），即将空闲司机派往刚刚流失请求的区域；以及预测式政策（A），即基于需求预测来规划司机移动。每个司机都是一个以最大化自身净收入为目标的LLM智能体，其条件为：不提供规则（N），或按该指令的详细程度提供规则（L）。我们在三区域模型和曼哈顿真实路网中测试了两个LLM——Claude Haiku 5.5和Jev，二者对规则的理解水平相当。结果显示，在规则被披露后，司机更紧密地遵循平台指令：在曼哈顿，他们拒绝调度提议的比例下降……
tldr: 该研究首次在欧盟《平台工作指令》强制披露算法规则的背景下，用以自身收益最大化为目标的自利LLM司机智能体评估网约车反应式与预测式两类调度政策，发现规则公开后司机更遵循平台调度指令、拒绝调度的比例显著下降。
en_tdlr: This paper evaluates ride-hailing rebalancing policies (reactive vs. anticipatory) using self-interested LLM driver agents under the EU Platform Work Directive's mandatory disclosure rules, finding that when the rules are disclosed, drivers follow the platform more closely and decline fewer relocation offers.
